title: Dynamic Risk Assessment

evidence.source_text: Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA) (see figure 10 ) is a simple risk assessment process...

nodes.text: Evaluate the situation, tasks, and persons at risk

evidence.source_text: Evaluate The Situation, Tasks and Persons at Risk

evidence.source_text: Determine the tasks and identify the associated hazards to determine the risk for the situation.

nodes.text: Assess the chosen systems of work

evidence.source_text: Assess the chosen systems of work

nodes.text: Are the risks proportional to the benefits?

evidence.source_text: Decide: Are the risk proportional to the benefits?

nodes.text: Assess whether the benefits outweigh the consequences

evidence.source_text: Determine whether the risks of the tasks are proportional to the benefits by assessing whether the benefit of carrying out the tasks outweigh the consequences if the risk was to occur.

When the risk of the system of work is not proportional to the benefits introduce risk controls using the risk control hierarchy of elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, personal protective equipment (PPE).
If the benefits outweigh the risks the task can proceed.
If the risks outweigh the benefits, DO NOT proceed with the tasks...
